description_full: The GPT Group is one of Australia's leading property groups, with assets under management of 34.1 billion US dollars across a portfolio of high quality retail, office and logistics assets. The GPT Group (GPT) is a stapled entity comprised of the General Property Trust (the Trust) and its controlled entities and GPT Management Holdings Limited (the Company) and its controlled entities. General Property Trust is a registered scheme, registered and domiciled in Australia. GPT RE Limited (GPTRE) is the Responsible Entity of the General Property Trust. GPT Management Holdings Limited (GPTMHL) is a company limited by shares, incorporated and domiciled in Australia. GPTRE Limited is a wholly owned entity of GPT Management Holdings Limited. The GPT Group was incorporated in 1959 in Australia.
ceo_bio: Mr. Russell  Proutt BComm CA CBV | CEO, MD & Board of Director | Compensation: $2.3M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: GPT Group is a mid-cap real estate business with a $6.3B market cap on $699M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 64% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $407M in free cash flow — roughly 58 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 8.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Remote work structural vacancy — the post-pandemic shift to hybrid work has permanently impaired demand for urban office space across most markets.
Climate and insurance cost escalation — rising premiums and coverage withdrawals in flood/fire zones are repricing assets that the market once treated as perpetuities.

news_headlines.title: The GPT Group (OTCMKTS:GPTGF) Sees Large Decline in Short Interest

sect: Its 62% operating margin runs 40pp above the Real Estate median (23%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.15x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.6% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 146 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 10% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 14% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 37% and a beta of 0.33, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $2K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 64% in the 2020 crash and 30% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 30% below its DCF fair value of $4.70, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 23%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $3.15 to $7.37 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Real Estate peers: P/E 8.9 vs 23.9 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.4% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 3.6% annual cash-flow growth, 8pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 6.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.13).
It runs a 64% gross margin and converts 58% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.6x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 8.4x net debt to EBITDA ($67.3M of cash against $3.7B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.8x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.16 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.25 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.1% over 3 years.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 59%.
It returns 4.9% a year to shareholders (5.1% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: CEO pay is $2.3M, and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
